summary.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.
demand_pricing: Management said export share rose to 10.4% and that new markets in South and West India are being developed; no export target given.
Pricing: management said starch margin is a whole-number (per-ton) business rather than percentage-based; a rise in starch prices would not proportionally lift EBITDA per ton.
Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.
About 70-80% of new modified starch volumes expected to go to existing paper-mill and food customers.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is the expanded plant running at and when will it reach a comfortable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is rising from the early-June start and expects maximum utilisation within the year; FY27 crushing expected above 4 lakh tons vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 47% PAT jump driven by raw material cost or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to operating leverage and the drop in low-margin trading from about 19% to about 3% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA per ton should be expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing maize and product price dependence; it expects per-ton EBITDA to improve with scale and value-add at constant prices (Q1 EBITDA/ton cited as about Rs 4,450 vs Rs 4,742 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest cost for FY27 after Bihar subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26; subvention runs across multiple project loans, with the Rs 40 crore cap still pending final policy.

qa_highlights.question: When will peak debt occur and when will working capital come down?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is peaking in H1 FY27 because working capital is highest then; debt expected to fall in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What production was lost in Q1 and is the value-added capacity stable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 shutdown days (approx. 7,200 MT lost). Liquid glucose at about 70% of capacity; maltodextrin needs 2-3 more months; modified starch trials to be online by September.

qa_highlights.question: Any new capex plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation and reduce debt before considering the next expansion.

risks_watch: Ramp-up risk: Q1 utilisation was 71.4% after about 9 shutdown days (about 7,200 MT lost); Q2 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons and FY27 to at least 4 lakh tons, and both depend on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Maltodextrin powder still needs 2-3 more months to reach target; modified starch trials are to be fully online by September 2026 and dextrose products are expected by about Q4 FY27.
Working capital and leverage: cash conversion cycle at 130 days, net debt Rs 735.32 crore, and debt expected to peak in H1 FY27 before falling in H2.

Interest subvention: the Bihar subvention cap was reportedly amended to Rs 40 crore, but the final policy notification was still awaited; the Rs 20 crore cap is still the one being applied in accounts.
Margin visibility: management declined to guide EBITDA per ton or margin, citing maize and product price dependence, so FY27 margin trajectory remains unquantified.
Maize price exposure: Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg versus market talk of Rs 24, with about 80% of annual requirement already bought in the Rabi season.
key_quotes: Q1 FY’27 was a quarter of transition.
So, what we can definitely guide is that we are going to grow our production and we will get operating leverage.
Sustainable at the moment, I cannot tell you, because we are at a time of transition.
It’s too early for us to talk about another next expansion. We are just stabilizing this one.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the expansion and export growth but cautious on numbers: it repeatedly declined to give EBITDA per ton, EBITDA margin, export targets, and FY28 capacity plans, citing price dependence and the need to stabilise the new plant first. Specific figures were given on crushing volumes, net interest cost and value-added share, while several answers (subvention amount, starch price trend, product margins) were deferred to the IR team.
